steps.message:
Item 051 on the Package A verification register is assigned to me and falls due on 07/20/2026, two days before the Level-3 placement. It covers the Block C spread footings and the long-term settlement of the clay beneath them.

Work through Item 051 against the project record and issue the verification memo. Set out what you reviewed, the basis you applied, your findings with the working behind them, and the disposition. Where something has to be produced before the item can be closed, say what it is and who is required to produce it.

Use the attached memorandum form and keep its sections. Write it from Rahul Nimkar, Geotechnical Reviewer, to Adrian Vance, Project Engineer, copied to Rachel Marlbeck. Save it as Thelbridge_Verification_Memo_Item051_BlockC.docx.

Adrian —

With the Level-3 concrete placement on 07/22/2026 approaching and several items still open on the Package A register, I want to confirm the position we agreed at award: no permanent work on Package A proceeds until Thelbridge has issued a written verification. That is the hold-point we set at Notice to Proceed, and it applies equally to the Level-3 pour and to every other operation on the current list.

Please close the current list — the shoring for the August Block B excavation, the pile downdrag question, the mat buoyancy check, Block C long-term settlement, this week's rebar lot and concrete breaks, the slab-on-grade compaction results, the podium deflection check, the basement seepage assessment, and the reinforcement cover on foundation and exterior work — and let me know by 07/20/2026 which are cleared and which are not.

If any item cannot be verified in time, we would rather delay the pour than release non-conforming work. I would appreciate a short written status against each item by end of day 07/20/2026 so that Steven and Gregory have a clean picture before the 07/22/2026 hold-point is either released or moved. If it is easier to walk me through it beforehand, I am available Monday afternoon.

Thank you.

Rachel

Adrian —

This is our formal pour-readiness notification for the Level-3 placement scheduled for 0530 on 07/22/2026. All test results for materials incorporated into this placement have been reviewed and are compliant. Specifically:

(a) Level-2 concrete 28-day cylinder reports issued 07/06/2026 — five sets, results confirm the mix.

(b) Slab-on-grade fill compaction report SF-26-0708 issued 07/09/2026 — all four tests exceed 95% requirement.

(c) Level-3 rebar lot 2026-0710 delivered 07/10/2026 — mill certificates on file (heats 4L2287, 4L2288, 4L2290, 4L2291), transmittal confirms conformance to ASTM A615/A615M-22 Grade 60.

(d) Pre-pour reinforcement and cover inspection completed 07/13/2026 — all elements comply with clear cover 1½ in per S-201.

Please issue the written verification releasing the hold-point no later than end of business 07/20/2026 so that we can confirm truck schedule with Haldenbrook.

Steven.

P 14 '' style Normal

P 17 'Set 3 of mix 03-CD-A is non-conforming to Specification 03 30 00 Article 3.7 and to ACI 318-19 §26.12.3.1.  1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

 Kelbrook Geotechnical, Inc. has completed a subsurface investigation and geotechnical engineering analysis for
 Package A of the Birchwood Village Expansion Program at 1802 Larchwood Avenue, Columbus, Ohio.
 Package A comprises three student-housing blocks (Blocks A, B and C) constructed over a shared podium, with
 a single basement level beneath Blocks A and B, and a separate deep plant-room excavation planned beneath
 Block B.
 The finished design grade across Package A is established at El. 750.0 ft. Existing ground surface stands at
 approximately El. 750.0 across the footprints of Blocks A and C but falls to about El. 738.0 across the Block B
 footprint (a former surface drainage swale). Placement of engineered fill of variable thickness — up to
 approximately 12 ft beneath Block B — will therefore be required to bring the site to design grade.
 The subsurface profile consists of three principal strata:
      • Stratum 1 — Upper sand, classified SP-SM (poorly-graded sand with silt), medium-dense, from
      existing grade down to El. 738.0, total unit weight 118 pcf.
      • Stratum 2 — Compressible clay aquitard, classified CL (lean clay of medium plasticity),
      normally-consolidated, from El. 738.0 down to El. 720.0 (18 ft thick), total unit weight 120 pcf, low
      permeability. This is the strata governing settlement of shallow foundations and provides the aquitard
      between the shallow and deep groundwater regimes.
      • Stratum 3 — Dense sand and gravel aquifer, classified SW-GW, below El. 720.0, total unit weight 130
      pcf, confined by the overlying clay.
 Groundwater is present as two distinct regimes:
      • The design water table in the upper sand is set at El. 742.0 ft. Piezometer readings taken from three
      shallow standpipes over the 11/2024–02/2025 monitoring period range from El. 741.6 to El. 742.4;
      groundwater seepage was observed at El. 741.8 to El. 742.2 in the Block A test-pit excavation.
      • A confined piezometric head of El. 738.0 ft has been measured in the deep sand-and-gravel aquifer
      through two deep piezometers screened below El. 720.0, with readings ranging El. 737.7 to El. 738.3. The
      confined head is at essentially the same elevation as the top of the clay aquitard.
 Consolidation testing on two undisturbed Shelby-tube samples of the compressible clay (samples B-06 U3 and
 B-08 U2, tested per ASTM D2435) yielded a compression index Cc = 0.28, a recompression index Cr = 0.045,
 an initial void ratio e0 = 0.92, an in-situ vertical effective stress σ'0 = 1,850 psf, and a preconsolidation pressure
 σ'p = 1,900 psf. The margin (σ'p − σ'0 ≈ 50 psf) confirms the clay is essentially normally-consolidated: any net
 stress increase applied at the top of the clay will produce virgin (Cc) compression rather than recompression
 (Cr) compression.
 Principal geotechnical recommendations are as follows:
       1. Block C — Spread footings may be founded within the upper sand. Consolidation of the underlying
       compressible clay under column-load stress increases at mid-depth of the clay must be explicitly computed
       by the Structural Engineer of Record, using the parameters provided herein, and reconciled against the
       settlement tolerances specified in the project structural criteria.
       2. Blocks A and B basement mat — A conventional reinforced-concrete mat foundation may be founded
       within the upper sand at the design underside elevation. Hydrostatic uplift from the El. 742.0 water table
       must be resolved by mat self-weight, superimposed permanent loads and, where necessary, tension
       elements. The waterproofing system for the below-grade envelope must be selected for the applicable

       hydrostatic head.
       3. Block B piles — Because of anticipated fill-induced consolidation of the underlying clay and the
       resulting downdrag loads, and because column loads at Block B exceed the safe capacity of shallow
       foundations bearing on the upper sand, closed-end driven pipe piles carried through the upper sand and the
       clay to bearing in the dense sand and gravel aquifer below El. 720.0 are recommended. The pile design
       must address soil-pile interaction from clay consolidation, as the engineered fill load induces downdrag on
       piles driven through the consolidating clay (Section 8.3).
       4. Block B plant-room excavation — The plant-room subgrade is planned near El. 726.0, i.e., inside the
       clay aquitard, approximately 6 ft above the top of the confined aquifer at El. 720.0. Because the confined
       piezometric head (El. 738.0) is approximately 12 ft above the planned subgrade elevation, this excavation
       will develop a significant uplift pressure on the clay plug from the underlying aquifer.
       The base-heave stability of the plug must be evaluated by the design team, and pressure-relief
       or aquifer-drawdown measures may be required. This condition is called out as the controlling
       constructability issue for the plant-room excavation and must be addressed by the Contractor’s dewatering
       and shoring designs.
       5. Engineered fill over the clay — The 12 ft of engineered fill required beneath Block B (from El. 738.0
       up to El. 750.0) will constitute a net surcharge on the normally-consolidated compressible clay across the
       Block B footprint. Because σ'p ≈ σ'0, the entire increment is virgin compression under Cc. The Owner is
       advised that consolidation of the underlying clay under this fill surcharge will occur, that the associated
       settlement will affect the behavior of any deep foundations driven from the raised working grade before
       the consolidation is substantially complete, and that these effects must be considered in the pile design.

 1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

 Kelbrook Geotechnical, Inc. has completed a subsurface investigation and geotechnical engineering analysis for
 Package A of the Birchwood Village Expansion Program at 1802 Larchwood Avenue, Columbus, Ohio.
 Package A comprises three student-housing blocks (Blocks A, B and C) constructed over a shared podium, with
 a single basement level beneath Blocks A and B, and a separate deep plant-room excavation planned beneath
 Block B.
 The finished design grade across Package A is established at El. 750.0 ft. Existing ground surface stands at
 approximately El. 750.0 across the footprints of Blocks A and C but falls to about El. 738.0 across the Block B
 footprint (a former surface drainage swale). Placement of engineered fill of variable thickness — up to
 approximately 12 ft beneath Block B — will therefore be required to bring the site to design grade.
 The subsurface profile consists of three principal strata:
      • Stratum 1 — Upper sand, classified SP-SM (poorly-graded sand with silt), medium-dense, from
      existing grade down to El. 738.0, total unit weight 118 pcf.
      • Stratum 2 — Compressible clay aquitard, classified CL (lean clay of medium plasticity),
      normally-consolidated, from El. 738.0 down to El. 720.0 (18 ft thick), total unit weight 120 pcf, low
      permeability. This is the strata governing settlement of shallow foundations and provides the aquitard
      between the shallow and deep groundwater regimes.
      • Stratum 3 — Dense sand and gravel aquifer, classified SW-GW, below El. 720.0, total unit weight 130
      pcf, confined by the overlying clay.
 Groundwater is present as two distinct regimes:
      • The design water table in the upper sand is set at El. 742.0 ft. Piezometer readings taken from three
      shallow standpipes over the 11/2024–02/2025 monitoring period range from El. 741.6 to El. 742.4;
      groundwater seepage was observed at El. 741.8 to El. 742.2 in the Block A test-pit excavation.
      • A confined piezometric head of El. 738.0 ft has been measured in the deep sand-and-gravel aquifer
      through two deep piezometers screened below El. 720.0, with readings ranging El. 737.7 to El. 738.3. The

 8. ENGINEERING ANALYSIS
 8.1 Consolidation of the Clay Aquitard
 The 18-ft-thick CL clay aquitard is normally-consolidated (Section 5.2). Any net stress increase q applied at
 the top of the clay will produce virgin, one-dimensional consolidation settlement along the Cc slope. In terms of
 the standard one-dimensional consolidation equation, in which Sc is the settlement and q the stress increase:
         Sc   = Cc · H / (1 + e0) · log10[ (σ'0 + q) / σ'0 ]

 with:
      • Cc = 0.28
      • e0 = 0.92
      • H (thickness of clay) = 18 ft
      • σ'0 = 1,850 psf at mid-depth of clay (El. 729)
 For any q > (σ'p − σ'0) ≈ 50 psf, virgin compression governs and the above expression applies. Because σ'p is
 only marginally above σ'0, this threshold is exceeded by essentially any structural or fill load of engineering
 interest.

 so that it is explicitly transmitted to the Structural Engineer of Record, the Contractor’s shoring designer and the
 Contractor’s dewatering designer at the earliest possible stage of design.

 8.3 Downdrag on Deep Foundations



 The Block B footprint is raised approximately 12 ft above its natural surface by engineered fill placed
 over a normally-consolidated CLAY 18 ft thick and of low permeability. Primary consolidation of that
 clay under the weight of the new fill was in progress at the date of this issue and, on the coefficients
 measured in the laboratory series, is expected to continue for a period measured in years rather than
 months.

 Deep foundations driven from the raised working grade pass through that consolidating layer. Where the
 surrounding soil settles more than the pile, the relative movement at the pile-soil interface reverses:
 the soil moves down past the shaft instead of the shaft moving down past the soil.


 Over the depth in which that condition applies the interface shear acts downward on the pile. It is an
 additional axial load carried by the pile, not a component of its resistance, and it is superimposed on
 the structural load for as long as consolidation continues.
 The magnitude depends on the thickness of the still-consolidating layer, the interface shear available
 within it and the depth of the neutral plane. Requirements for its treatment in design are set out in
 Section 9.3.

   1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE
   This memorandum establishes the governing codes, reference standards, site parameters, design loads, load
   combinations, and serviceability criteria adopted for the structural design of Package A of the Birchwood Village
   Expansion. Package A comprises three student-housing blocks (Blocks A, B and C) constructed over a shared

   6. LOAD COMBINATIONS
   Strength design (LRFD) load combinations for gravity, wind, and seismic follow ASCE 7-16 §2.3.1. Allowable
   stress combinations (ASD) per §2.4 are used only for soil-structure interaction checks at the geotechnical
   interface (bearing pressure, settlement) and are stated in the geotechnical calculation package. Load combinations
   relevant to Package A are set out in full below.

   6.1 Basic Strength Load Combinations — ASCE 7-16 §2.3.1
           (1) 1.4D
           (2) 1.2D + 1.6L + 0.5(Lr or S or R)
           (3) 1.2D + 1.6(Lr or S or R) + (L or 0.5W)
           (4) 1.2D + 1.0W + L + 0.5(Lr or S or R)
           (5) 1.2D + Ev + Eh + L + 0.2S
           (6) 0.9D + 1.0W
           (7) 0.9D − Ev + Eh
   Where:
         D = dead load; L = live load; Lr = roof live; S = snow; R = rain; W = wind; E = earthquake with vertical Ev =
         0.2·SDS·D and horizontal Eh = ρ·QE component.

   6.2 Counteracting Combinations — ASCE 7-16 §2.3.1(6)–(7)
   Combinations (6) and (7) — 0.9D + W and 0.9D − E + E — apply where the dead load counteracts (rather than
   compounds) the effect of the variable load. These combinations apply
   to the applicable stability check.

   This governs:
         • Flotation and uplift. A permanent load that resists overturning, sliding, uplift or flotation
         is taken at 0.9D, with an explicit factor of safety stated; minimum 1.5 for sliding and base heave.



         • Overturning of shear walls. Wind and seismic overturning at Blocks A, B and C shear walls, and at
         podium transfer walls, are checked with 0.9D on the resisting side.
         • Uplift on Block B piles under wind and seismic. Piles are checked for reversal per §12.13 with 0.9D on
         the gravity leg.
   The design basis for each element applies the appropriate combination
   on the corresponding sheet of the calculation package.

         • D + 0.7E (drift check under seismic)
         • Sustained (D + long-term L) with the ACI 318-19 §24.2.4 long-term multiplier applied

• Settlement Monitoring — Block C, readings through 06/26/2026 (Monitoring
  Points, Readings, Trend Chart and Notes sheets).
• Baseline, cumulative readings, interval changes, survey controls and construction/loading
  history.
• Sheet S-101, Foundation Plan, Rev.4, issued 05/29/2026.
• Confirms Block C is founded on spread footings, without a basement.
 3. BASIS OF REVIEW
Review was made on service (unfactored) foundation loads, using the assigned stress increase
at the clay mid-depth and the laboratory-derived one-dimensional consolidation properties. The
governing comparison is predicted total settlement ≤ 1.0 in and differential settlement ≤ 0.5 in
over 30 ft (Spec. 31 20 00 §3.6.A; DBM §7.3). Clay compression is calculated using Cc = 0.28,
Cr = 0.045, e₀ = 0.92, σ′₀ = 1,850 psf, σ′p = 1,900 psf and H = 18 ft. Immediate settlement
and consolidation are separate contributions; monitoring is a check on actual performance, not
a substitute for a completed long-term prediction.


4. FINDINGS
Findings are limited to the design and monitoring record listed above:
Finding 1 — Subsurface and loading basis. Kelbrook identifies an 18-ft normally
consolidated CL clay aquitard from El. 738 to El. 720 beneath Block C; Table 5-1 reports σ′₀ =
1,850 psf, σ′p = 1,900 psf, Cc = 0.28, Cr = 0.045 and e₀ = 0.92 (GIR pp. 11, 14–16; Vantree
VMT-2025-0109-CON). CB-GEO-007 Sheet 2 reports Δσ = 900 psf at clay mid-depth from its
footing stress superposition (Sheet 2, rows 39–41). OCR = 1,900/1,850 = 1.027; final effective
stress at the calculation point is 1,850 + 900 = 2,750 psf, 850 psf above σ′p. A virgin-
compression settlement check is therefore required.
Finding 2 — Issued calculation omits consolidation. CB-GEO-007 Sheet 3 reports a
maximum immediate settlement of 0.90 in and labels its comparison “maximum total
settlement”; however, the method there is an immediate Schmertmann elastic calculation.
Sheet 4 explicitly states “Not computed” and that serviceability is taken from Sheet 3. Sheet 5
lists the clay parameters and 900 psf increment but does not perform a consolidation
computation. Consequently the 0.90-in result is not a total-settlement verification, and the
Sheet 3 differential result (0.20 in) is not a long-term differential check.
Finding 3 — Independent long-term computation exceeds tolerance. Using the GIR §8.1
normally-consolidated expression: Sc = Cc·H/(1+e₀)·log₁₀[(σ′₀+Δσ)/σ′₀] =
0.28·18/(1+0.92)·log₁₀(2,750/1,850) = 0.4519 ft = 5.42 in of consolidation settlement alone. As
a check using Vantree’s Cr for the initial 50-psf recompression segment and Cc thereafter: Sc
= H/(1+e₀)·[Cr·log₁₀(1,900/1,850) + Cc·log₁₀(2,750/1,900)] = 0.4264 ft = 5.12 in. Both
approaches exceed the 1.0-in total tolerance before adding any immediate settlement. Adding
CB-GEO-007’s 0.90-in immediate estimate only as a separate indicative component gives
approximately 6.02–6.32 in; it is not offered as an accepted EOR total.

footing-by-footing consolidation results, so the additional differential settlement cannot be
established from CB-GEO-007. The latest record is the 06/26/2026 round: maximum
cumulative downward movement is 0.61 in at MP-7/FTG-C7; minimum is 0.31 in at MP-12, a
0.30-in range over approximately 35.4 ft. The largest adjacent-point difference is 0.23 in across
a 26-ft grid spacing. The recorded values are presently below the 1.0-in total and 0.5-in
differential limits; however, the 0.61-in maximum is already 61% of the total limit and is not
stable. At MP-7, the last 14-day increment is 0.07 in (0.005 in/day), up from 0.06 in/14 days
(0.0043 in/day) in the preceding interval. The monitoring workbook notes that the rate is not
yet decreasing (Readings, rows 18–19 and 36–37; Trend Chart and Notes). Kelbrook expects

evidence of ongoing response, not a final-settlement prediction; they are not added to the full
predicted settlement because the baselines and load history differ.

VERIFICATION MEMORANDUM
To: Adrian Vance, Project Engineer (Structural/Geotechnical), Owner’s
Representative
From: Rahul Nimkar, Geotechnical Reviewer
Date: 07/20/2026
Subject: Item 051 — Block C spread-footing long-term settlement verification

cc: Rachel Marlbeck, University Program Director
Project: Birchwood Village Expansion Program — Package A

1. PURPOSE
This memorandum addresses Verification Register Item 051, assigned to the Geotechnical
Reviewer and due 07/20/2026. It determines whether the Block C spread-footing design
calculation demonstrates compliance with long-term total and differential settlement criteria
over the compressible clay, and whether the available settlement monitoring supports that
determination.


2. DOCUMENTS REVIEWED
The following project-record documents were reviewed:
 • Thelbridge Verification Register — Package A, last updated 07/15/2026, REGISTER
   sheet, Item 051. Item 051 records the 18-ft clay layer, 900 psf mid-layer stress increase,
   1.0-in total / 0.5-in differential criteria, and required correlation to monitoring.
• Geotechnical Investigation Report — Package A, Rev.2, 02/14/2025, §§5.2, 8.1 and
  9.1 (report pp. 11, 14–16). Subsurface profile, consolidation equation and Block C
  foundation recommendations.
• Vantree Materials Testing, Laboratory Consolidation Test Report VMT-2025-0109-
  CON, 01/09/2025 (ASTM D2435), samples B-06 U3 and B-08 U2. Laboratory
  consolidation parameters used in the independent calculation.
• Calloway Braddock calculation CB-GEO-007, Block C Spread Footing Settlement,
  issued 09/30/2025, Sheets 2–5. Footing service loads, stated 900 psf stress increase,
  immediate settlement analysis and consolidation sheet.
• Design Basis Memorandum CB-DBM-001, Rev.2, 11/14/2025, §7.3 (p. 8). Block C
  serviceability criteria and requirement to check clay settlement.
• Specification Section 31 20 00, Earth Moving, Rev.3, 03/06/2026, §3.6 (p. 5).
  Contract settlement tolerances, monitoring and response to predicted or measured
  exceedance.
• Settlement Monitoring — Block C, readings through 06/26/2026 (Monitoring
  Points, Readings, Trend Chart and Notes sheets). Baseline, cumulative readings,
  interval changes, survey controls and construction/loading history.
• Sheet S-101, Foundation Plan, Rev.4, issued 05/29/2026. Confirms Block C is founded
  on spread footings, without a basement.


3. BASIS OF REVIEW
Review was made on service (unfactored) foundation loads, using the assigned stress increase
at the clay mid-depth and the laboratory-derived one-dimensional consolidation properties. The
governing comparison is predicted total settlement ≤ 1.0 in and differential settlement ≤ 0.5 in
over 30 ft (Spec. 31 20 00 §3.6.A; DBM §7.3); the calculation cover also states an angular-
 distortion limit of 1/500 (CB-GEO-007, Cover, Sheet 1). Clay compression is calculated using
Cc = 0.28, Cr = 0.045, e₀ = 0.92, σ′₀ = 1,850 psf, σ′p = 1,900 psf and H = 18 ft. Immediate
settlement and consolidation are separate contributions; monitoring is a check on actual
performance, not a substitute for a completed long-term prediction.


4. FINDINGS
Findings are limited to the design and monitoring record listed above:
Finding 1 — Subsurface and loading basis. Kelbrook identifies an 18-ft normally
consolidated CL clay aquitard from El. 738 to El. 720 beneath Block C; Table 5-1 reports σ′₀ =
1,850 psf, σ′p = 1,900 psf, Cc = 0.28, Cr = 0.045 and e₀ = 0.92 (GIR pp. 11, 14–16; Vantree
VMT-2025-0109-CON). CB-GEO-007 Sheet 2 reports Δσ = 900 psf at clay mid-depth from its
footing stress superposition (Sheet 2, rows 39–41). OCR = 1,900/1,850 = 1.027; final effective
stress at the calculation point is 1,850 + 900 = 2,750 psf, 850 psf above σ′p. A virgin-
compression settlement check is therefore required. Sheet 2 reports the Boussinesq/Newmark
superposition of four adjacent footings with a 2:1 method verification, but shows the 900 psf
result without the point-by-point stress factors/calculation; I have treated 900 psf as the
calculation’s stated input, not independently validated it.
Finding 2 — Issued calculation omits consolidation. CB-GEO-007 Sheet 3 reports a
maximum immediate settlement of 0.90 in and labels its comparison “maximum total
settlement”; however, the method there is an immediate Schmertmann elastic calculation.
Sheet 4 explicitly states “Not computed” and that serviceability is taken from Sheet 3. Sheet 5
lists the clay parameters and 900 psf increment but does not perform a consolidation
computation. Consequently the 0.90-in result is not a total-settlement verification, and the
Sheet 3 differential result (0.20 in) is not a long-term differential check.
Finding 3 — Independent long-term computation exceeds tolerance. Using the GIR §8.1
normally-consolidated expression: Sc = Cc·H/(1+e₀)·log₁₀[(σ′₀+Δσ)/σ′₀] =
0.28·18/(1+0.92)·log₁₀(2,750/1,850) = 0.4519 ft = 5.42 in of consolidation settlement alone. As
a check using Vantree’s Cr for the initial 50-psf recompression segment and Cc thereafter: Sc
= H/(1+e₀)·[Cr·log₁₀(1,900/1,850) + Cc·log₁₀(2,750/1,900)] = 0.4264 ft = 5.12 in. Both
approaches exceed the 1.0-in total tolerance before adding any immediate settlement. Adding
CB-GEO-007’s 0.90-in immediate estimate only as a separate indicative component gives
approximately 6.02–6.32 in; it is not offered as an accepted EOR total.
Finding 4 — Differential and time response are unresolved. The workbook provides no
footing-by-footing consolidation results, so the additional differential settlement and long-term
angular distortion cannot be established from CB-GEO-007. The latest record available as of
this memorandum is the 06/26/2026 round: maximum cumulative downward movement is 0.61
in at MP-7/FTG-C7; minimum is 0.31 in at MP-12, a 0.30-in range over approximately 35.4 ft.
The largest adjacent-point difference is 0.23 in across a 26-ft grid spacing. The recorded values
are presently below the 1.0-in total and 0.5-in differential limits; however, the 0.61-in
maximum is already 61% of the total limit and is not stable. At MP-7, the last 14-day increment
is 0.07 in (0.005 in/day), up from 0.06 in/14 days (0.0043 in/day) in the preceding interval. The
monitoring workbook notes that the rate is not yet decreasing (Readings, rows 18–19 and 36–
37; Trend Chart and Notes). Kelbrook expects primary consolidation to continue over years
(GIR §8.1, p. 15). The 06/26 readings are evidence of ongoing response, not a final-settlement
prediction; they are not added to the full predicted settlement because the baselines and load
history differ.
 5. CONCLUSION AND RECOMMENDATION
Thelbridge disposition: NOT VERIFIED. Item 051 remains OPEN; the record does not
demonstrate compliance with the long-term settlement criteria. The omitted consolidation
component is material and the independent calculation exceeds the total-settlement tolerance.
No closure or settlement clearance is recommended on the current submittal.
• Required before closure — EOR calculation and disposition. Gregory Nash, PE,
  Calloway Braddock (Structural Engineer of Record), shall issue a revised, signed/sealed CB-
  GEO-007 that shows the working substantiating the 900 psf Boussinesq/Newmark stress
  increase (and confirms it against current Block C footing geometry and loads), explicitly
  computes long-term consolidation for the governing Block C footing(s), and reconciles
  immediate plus consolidation settlement to total and differential limits (including the 0.5 in
  over 30 ft and 1/500 angular-distortion criteria). The revision must explain the treatment of
  σ′p/Cr/Cc and time-dependent consolidation, and address the actual monitoring record. If
  either tolerance is exceeded, the EOR must provide a written design disposition and
  mitigation/revised foundation design (as applicable) for geotechnical review; a spreadsheet
  parameter listing alone is insufficient. Kelbrook Geotechnical should provide any additional
  soil interpretation requested by the EOR.
• Required before closure — current survey. Rowan Bay Constructors shall have its
  surveyor/Party Chief, Dennis Halloran, PLS, obtain and submit an updated Block C
  monitoring round after 06/26/2026, with reduced elevations and cumulative settlement at all
  12 points, interval movements/rates, and differential comparisons. The existing 14-day
  record cadence should be maintained pending a written disposition; the last reading
  presently in the record is 24 days before this memo.
• Interim control. Under Specification 31 20 00 §3.6.B, because the predicted settlement
  exceeds the tolerance, notify the EOR in writing and apply no additional load to the Block C
  foundation system until the EOR issues a written disposition. Continue readings under
  §3.6.C. This Item 051 memorandum is not a release of any separate Package A hold-point.

Subject: Item 051 — Block C spread-footing long-term settlement verification

cc: Rachel Marlbeck, University Program Director
Project: Birchwood Village Expansion Program — Package A

1. PURPOSE
This memorandum addresses Verification Register Item 051, assigned to the Geotechnical
Reviewer and due 07/20/2026. It determines whether the Block C spread-footing design
calculation demonstrates compliance with long-term total and differential settlement criteria
over the compressible clay, and whether the available settlement monitoring supports that
determination.


2. DOCUMENTS REVIEWED
The following project-record documents were reviewed:
 • Thelbridge Verification Register — Package A, last updated 07/15/2026, REGISTER
   sheet, Item 051. Item 051 records the 18-ft clay layer, 900 psf mid-layer stress increase,
   1.0-in total / 0.5-in differential criteria, and required correlation to monitoring.
• Geotechnical Investigation Report — Package A, Rev.2, 02/14/2025, §§5.2, 8.1 and
  9.1 (report pp. 11, 14–16). Subsurface profile, consolidation equation and Block C
  foundation recommendations.
• Vantree Materials Testing, Laboratory Consolidation Test Report VMT-2025-0109-
  CON, 01/09/2025 (ASTM D2435), samples B-06 U3 and B-08 U2. Laboratory
  consolidation parameters used in the independent calculation.
• Calloway Braddock calculation CB-GEO-007, Block C Spread Footing Settlement,
  issued 09/30/2025, Sheets 2–5. Footing service loads, stated 900 psf stress increase,
  immediate settlement analysis and consolidation sheet.
• Design Basis Memorandum CB-DBM-001, Rev.2, 11/14/2025, §7.3 (p. 8). Block C
  serviceability criteria and requirement to check clay settlement.
• Specification Section 31 20 00, Earth Moving, Rev.3, 03/06/2026, §3.6 (p. 5).
  Contract settlement tolerances, monitoring and response to predicted or measured
  exceedance.
• Settlement Monitoring — Block C, readings through 06/26/2026 (Monitoring
  Points, Readings, Trend Chart and Notes sheets). Baseline, cumulative readings,
  interval changes, survey controls and construction/loading history.
• Sheet S-101, Foundation Plan, Rev.4, issued 05/29/2026. Confirms Block C is founded
  on spread footings, without a basement.
 3. BASIS OF REVIEW
Review was made on service (unfactored) foundation loads, using the assigned stress increase
at the clay mid-depth and the laboratory-derived one-dimensional consolidation properties. The
governing comparison is predicted total settlement ≤ 1.0 in and differential settlement ≤ 0.5 in
over 30 ft (Spec. 31 20 00 §3.6.A; DBM §7.3); the calculation cover also states an angular-
distortion limit of 1/500 (CB-GEO-007, Cover, Sheet 1). Clay compression is calculated using
Cc = 0.28, Cr = 0.045, e₀ = 0.92, σ′₀ = 1,850 psf, σ′p = 1,900 psf and H = 18 ft. Immediate
settlement and consolidation are separate contributions; monitoring is a check on actual
performance, not a substitute for a completed long-term prediction.


4. FINDINGS
Findings are limited to the design and monitoring record listed above:
Finding 1 — Subsurface and loading basis. Kelbrook identifies an 18-ft normally
consolidated CL clay aquitard from El. 738 to El. 720 beneath Block C; Table 5-1 reports σ′₀ =
1,850 psf, σ′p = 1,900 psf, Cc = 0.28, Cr = 0.045 and e₀ = 0.92 (GIR pp. 11, 14–16; Vantree
VMT-2025-0109-CON). CB-GEO-007 Sheet 2 reports Δσ = 900 psf at clay mid-depth from its
footing stress superposition (Sheet 2, rows 39–41). OCR = 1,900/1,850 = 1.027; final effective
stress at the calculation point is 1,850 + 900 = 2,750 psf, 850 psf above σ′p. A virgin-
compression settlement check is therefore required. Sheet 2 reports the Boussinesq/Newmark
superposition of four adjacent footings with a 2:1 method verification, but shows the 900 psf
result without the point-by-point stress factors/calculation; I have treated 900 psf as the
calculation’s stated input, not independently validated it.
Finding 2 — Current footing geometry does not match the calculation. CB-GEO-007
Sheet 2 uses an assumed footing underside at El. 740.5 and lists 10.5 ft × 10.5 ft interior
footings (including governing F-C6); Sheet 3 models F-C6 as 10.5 ft × 10.5 ft. The current
issued foundation detail S-201 Rev.4, Detail 3, shows the typical Block C interior footing as 7 ft
6 in × 7 ft 6 in, with top at El. 748.0 and underside at El. 746.0. The calculation also
references a prior structural model Rev.A and S-101 Rev.2. The current EOR record does not
reconcile this difference to the foundation as constructed or establish that the 900 psf stress
increase and settlement results represent the current/as-built footing geometry. The EOR must
identify governing/as-built footing sizes, elevations and loads and revise the stress distribution
and settlement check accordingly.
Finding 3 — Issued calculation omits consolidation. CB-GEO-007 Sheet 3 reports a
maximum immediate settlement of 0.90 in and labels its comparison “maximum total
settlement”; however, the method there is an immediate Schmertmann elastic calculation.
Sheet 4 explicitly states “Not computed” and that serviceability is taken from Sheet 3. Sheet 5
lists the clay parameters and 900 psf increment but does not perform a consolidation
computation. Consequently the 0.90-in result is not a total-settlement verification, and the
Sheet 3 differential result (0.20 in) is not a long-term differential check.
Finding 4 — Independent long-term computation exceeds tolerance. Using the GIR §8.1
normally-consolidated expression: Sc = Cc·H/(1+e₀)·log₁₀[(σ′₀+Δσ)/σ′₀] =
0.28·18/(1+0.92)·log₁₀(2,750/1,850) = 0.4519 ft = 5.42 in of consolidation settlement alone. As
a check using Vantree’s Cr for the initial 50-psf recompression segment and Cc thereafter: Sc
= H/(1+e₀)·[Cr·log₁₀(1,900/1,850) + Cc·log₁₀(2,750/1,900)] = 0.4264 ft = 5.12 in. Both
approaches exceed the 1.0-in total tolerance before adding any immediate settlement. Adding
CB-GEO-007’s 0.90-in immediate estimate only as a separate indicative component gives
approximately 6.02–6.32 in; it is not offered as an accepted EOR total.
 Finding 5 — Differential and time response are unresolved. The workbook provides no
footing-by-footing consolidation results, so the additional differential settlement and long-term
angular distortion cannot be established from CB-GEO-007. The latest record available as of
this memorandum is the 06/26/2026 round: maximum cumulative downward movement is 0.61
in at MP-7/FTG-C7; minimum is 0.31 in at MP-12, a 0.30-in range over approximately 35.4 ft.
The largest adjacent-point difference is 0.23 in across a 26-ft grid spacing. The recorded values
are presently below the 1.0-in total and 0.5-in differential limits; however, the 0.61-in
maximum is already 61% of the total limit and is not stable. At MP-7, the last 14-day increment
is 0.07 in (0.005 in/day), up from 0.06 in/14 days (0.0043 in/day) in the preceding interval. The
monitoring workbook notes that the rate is not yet decreasing (Readings, rows 18–19 and 36–
37; Trend Chart and Notes). Kelbrook expects primary consolidation to continue over years
(GIR §8.1, p. 15). The 06/26 readings are evidence of ongoing response, not a final-settlement
prediction; they are not added to the full predicted settlement because the baselines and load
history differ.
 5. CONCLUSION AND RECOMMENDATION
Thelbridge disposition: NOT VERIFIED. Item 051 remains OPEN; the record does not
demonstrate compliance with the long-term settlement criteria. The omitted consolidation
component is material and the independent calculation exceeds the total-settlement tolerance.
No closure or settlement clearance is recommended on the current submittal.

  Rev.4 Detail 3, establishes the governing/as-built Block C footing dimensions, elevations and
  loads, shows the working substantiating the 900 psf Boussinesq/Newmark stress increase
  (or recalculates it using the resolved geometry), explicitly computes long-term consolidation

  criteria). The revision must explain the treatment of σ′p/Cr/Cc and time-dependent
  consolidation, and address the actual monitoring record. If either tolerance is exceeded, the
  EOR must provide a written design disposition and mitigation/revised foundation design (as
  applicable) for geotechnical review; a spreadsheet parameter listing alone is insufficient.
  Kelbrook Geotechnical should provide any additional soil interpretation requested by the
  EOR.
• Required before closure — current survey. Rowan Bay Constructors shall have its
  surveyor/Party Chief, Dennis Halloran, PLS, obtain and submit an updated Block C
  monitoring round after 06/26/2026, with reduced elevations and cumulative settlement at all
  12 points, interval movements/rates, and differential comparisons. The existing 14-day
  record cadence should be maintained pending a written disposition; the last reading
  presently in the record is 24 days before this memo.
• Interim control. Under Specification 31 20 00 §3.6.B, because the predicted settlement
  exceeds the tolerance, notify the EOR in writing and apply no additional load to the Block C
  foundation system until the EOR issues a written disposition. Continue readings under
  §3.6.C. This Item 051 memorandum is not a release of any separate Package A hold-point.

3. BASIS OF REVIEW
Review was made on service (unfactored) foundation loads, using the assigned stress increase
at the clay mid-depth and the laboratory-derived one-dimensional consolidation properties. The
governing comparison is predicted total settlement ≤ 1.0 in and differential settlement ≤ 0.5 in
over 30 ft (Spec. 31 20 00 §3.6.A; DBM §7.3); the calculation cover also states an angular-
distortion limit of 1/500 (CB-GEO-007, Cover, Sheet 1). Clay compression is calculated using
Cc = 0.28, Cr = 0.045, e₀ = 0.92, σ′₀ = 1,850 psf, σ′p = 1,900 psf and H = 18 ft. Immediate
settlement and consolidation are separate contributions; monitoring is a check on actual
...
Finding 4 — Independent long-term computation exceeds tolerance. Using the GIR §8.1
normally-consolidated expression: Sc = Cc·H/(1+e₀)·log₁₀[(σ′₀+Δσ)/σ′₀] =
0.28·18/(1+0.92)·log₁₀(2,750/1,850) = 0.4519 ft = 5.42 in of consolidation settlement alone. As
a check using Vantree’s Cr for the initial 50-psf recompression segment and Cc thereafter: Sc
= H/(1+e₀)·[Cr·log₁₀(1,900/1,850) + Cc·log₁₀(2,750/1,900)] = 0.4264 ft = 5.12 in. Both
approaches exceed the 1.0-in total tolerance before adding any immediate settlement. Adding
CB-GEO-007’s 0.90-in immediate estimate only as a separate indicative component gives
approximately 6.02–6.32 in; it is not offered as an accepted EOR total.

footing-by-footing consolidation results, so the additional differential settlement and long-term
angular distortion cannot be established from CB-GEO-007. The latest record available as of

in at MP-7/FTG-C7; minimum is 0.31 in at MP-12, a 0.30-in range over approximately 35.4 ft.

presently below the 1.0-in total and 0.5-in differential limits; however, the 0.61-in maximum is

monitoring workbook notes that the rate is not yet decreasing (Readings, rows 18–19 and 36–
37; Trend Chart and Notes). Kelbrook expects primary consolidation to continue over years

prediction; they are not added to the full predicted settlement because the baselines and load

Completed the verification memorandum using the attached form and saved it at:

`/filesystem/Thelbridge_Verification_Memo_Item051_BlockC.docx`

The memo’s disposition is **NOT VERIFIED; Item 051 remains OPEN**. CB-GEO-007 leaves consolidation uncomputed; using its stated 900 psf stress increase, the independent clay-consolidation check is about **5.42 in** (or **5.12 in** when accounting for the initial recompression segment), exceeding the 1.0-in total-settlement limit before adding immediate settlement. The memo also flags the difference between the calculation’s footing geometry and current S-201 Rev.4, and the ongoing monitoring trend.

Before closure, it identifies the need for a revised, signed/sealed calculation and written design disposition from **Gregory Nash, PE**, and an updated monitoring survey from **Rowan Bay Constructors’ surveyor/Party Chief Dennis Halloran, PLS**. The DOCX was reopened and checked; its five form sections are present.
